The evidence doesn't show that. It can't say what caused the 2025 loss.

What it does show: Hansen/UMD mapped about 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025 inside ASSET-F (3.91% of the 345.6 ha property). The JRC 2020 map agrees that 98% of that area was forest in 2020. The MGAP 2021 map classes about 13.1 ha as native forest, none as planted, and 0.4 ha as outside mapped forest.

What it doesn't establish: the cause (clearing, harvest, fire, storm), whether deforestation or a land-use change occurred, legality, or who is responsible. The native forest classification is territorial context, not a cause.

The finding is also still pending corroboration. 2025 is the latest year in the series, so no later year yet shows whether the loss persisted.

To test the agricultural-clearing hypothesis, you'd need 2026 data to see what follows the loss (for example, crops or pasture), plus higher-resolution imagery or field and permit records.
